resale_co.name: Property Transfer (Resale) Inspection
resale_co.issued_by: Division of Housing, Ewing Township Code Enforcement Office (Construction Office)
requirements: Exterior property: sanitation, grading and drainage, sidewalks and driveways, weeds, rodent harborage, garage, shed, fences and walls, motor vehicles
Exterior structure: doors, windows, trim and porches, street numbers, foundation, roof and drains, chimneys, stairs and decks, working windows and insect screens
Interior: structural members, stairs, railings and handrails, rubbish and garbage storage, insect or rodent infestation, lighting and ventilation
Plumbing: fixtures, water system, drainage, water pressure and hot water temperature
Heating and mechanical equipment, combustion air and clearances
Electrical: at least 2 receptacles per bedroom and GFCI outlets in kitchen, bath and outdoors
Smoke alarm on every level (10 year lithium sealed battery single station alarms)
Carbon monoxide alarm within 10 feet of sleeping areas
Well water certificate if the home has a well
All open permits must be closed out; some repairs may need construction (UCC) permits
A Tax Assessor representative comes to the home on the day of the inspection

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Property Transfer Resale Application (owner, buyer, property details and the number of smoke and CO detectors) and submit it with the fee to the Ewing Construction Office, 1666 Pennington Rd. (rear of building), Ewing. The form has boxes for cash, check or credit card, and asks whether the certificate should be picked up, mailed or emailed. The form says an LLC seller or buyer must also list the owner's name. Inspections can also be requested and tracked on the Township's SDL Portal (account needed).

resale_co.notes: The Division of Housing inspects every dwelling offered for resale under Township ordinance and the International Property Maintenance Code. The Township code (ecode360 EW1628) could not be opened, so the lead time, how long the certificate is valid, and any reinspection fee were not confirmed. Search summaries describe the code as requiring an inspection within 15 working days of the application, with the Tax Assessor attending, but the exact ordinance text was not seen. The Township website sometimes shows a 'One moment, please' loading page to automated requests; the pages and PDFs here were read when they loaded normally. The office phone (609) 883-2900 is from the Housing page, which lists Lisa Litz at x7677; the application form lists Ext 7676 (Office Clerk Amy Mostrangeli, amostrangeli@ewingnj.org). Landlords need a separate rental registration and a Property Maintenance Inspection on each tenant change (not a sale requirement).

requirements: Ten-year sealed battery single station smoke alarms are required for any residential property transfer
Hardwired (A.C. powered) smoke alarms may not be replaced with battery alarms
The 2025 property transfer information form says a fire extinguisher is no longer required for residential properties

authorities.name: Ewing Township Fire Prevention (municipal local enforcing agency); smoke and CO alarms are also checked in the Division of Housing property transfer inspection
authorities.how_to_apply: No separate smoke and carbon monoxide certificate application or fee is posted. The Housing resale application asks for the number of smoke and CO detectors, and the property transfer information form lists smoke and CO alarms among the items inspected. Call Fire Prevention or the Code Enforcement Office to confirm whether the certificate is issued with the resale inspection or needs its own request and fee.

fire_cert.notes: The state registry lists Ewing Township (municipality) as the fire code enforcing agency, and the state directory names Fire Official Chad Hutchinson with 'Ewing Twp Fire Prev' as the smoke detector compliance office. The Township Fire Prevention page describes its inspections as commercial buildings and common areas of multiple dwellings, while the Housing page covers resale inspections of all dwellings, so the smoke and CO check for a 1-2 family sale appears to happen in the Housing property transfer inspection. This was not stated outright. The Construction staff page still lists Mike Nelson as Fire Marshal at (609) 882-9885 x112 (with a misspelled email), while the Fire Prevention page names Chad Hutchinson as Acting Fire Marshal at the same extension; the Fire Prevention page and the state directory were used. The Housing page still says a portable fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen is required, but the 2025 transfer information form says it is no longer required for residential properties.
